unresolved.question: Page legend (even-page style) defines only digits: ১ এক আলিফ, circled ১ দম ফেলিলে এক আলিফ, ২ দম ফেলিলে দুই আলিফ, ৩ তিন আলিফ, ৪ চার আলিফ, ৬ দম ফেলিলে তিন / না ফেলিলে এক; letter signs use the default labels.
Every band ২ on this page (rows 0, 2, 5, 6, 8, 9) sits over a noon sakin before an ikhfa letter, not over a madd; labelled with the legend text for ২ (দম ফেলিলে দুই আলিফ) anyway.

Row 3: the three band signs over اللّٰهُ are printed tightly together (ringed-wedge, ৬, ম); the middle one is read as a plain ৬ and, with ম, placed on the lam carrying the superscript alif; the ringed-wedge on the final ه.

Row 3: a solid down arrow is printed in the band above the 74:56 verse circle (end of Surah 74); recorded on the last letter of الْمَغْفِرَةِ. The right-margin box beside rows 2-3 reads 'তিন চতুর্থাংশ পারা' with an arrow, so the arrow is taken as the three-quarter para mark and labelled with that note (interpretation, not a legend entry).

Row 9: the first يَوْمَئِذِ has a single kasra under ذ and a small noon with its own kasra printed above-left (nun qutni); encoded as kasra + U+06E8 (ۨ), the noon's kasra cannot be encoded separately. The solid down arrow above it is labelled from the right-margin note beside rows 8-9 (paraphrased: when stopping the noon is not read; otherwise read the noon with kasra joined to the following sakin).

Row 9: a second solid down arrow is printed in the band beside the ringed-wedge over the 75:12 verse circle; recorded on the last letter of الْمُسْتَقَرُّ with the catalog label. A second right-margin note beside row 9 is cut off at the page edge and unreadable.
Row 9: the second يَوْمَئِذٍ carries a small meem (iqlab) above the kasratan on ذ, with band গ; encoded ذٍۢ.
Row 4: the Bengali prints 'আত্ম-ভৎর্সনাকারী' (sic) and is transcribed as printed.
